theory.intro: A growing pattern can be recorded in a table of values, linking the step number to the number of items used.
facts: Each row of the pattern gives a pair: the **step number** and the **count**.
If each step adds the same amount, the counts have a **constant increase**.
A table makes the connection between the two quantities easy to see.
steps: Count the items in the first few steps of the pattern.
Record each step number and its count as a column in the table.
Continue the pattern to fill in further values.

workedExamples.question_text:
Each stage has as many separate squares as its stage number. Each square uses $4$ matchsticks; squares do not share matchsticks.

[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[x=7mm,y=7mm,draw=black,text=black,line width=0.6pt]\draw (0,0) rectangle (1,1);\draw (3,0) rectangle (4,1);\draw (4.4,0) rectangle (5.4,1);\draw (7,0) rectangle (8,1);\draw (8.4,0) rectangle (9.4,1);\draw (9.8,0) rectangle (10.8,1);\path (0.5,-0.5) node[font=\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont]{Stage 1};\path (4.2,-0.5) node[font=\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont]{Stage 2};\path (8.9,-0.5) node[font=\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont]{Stage 3};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]

Complete the table through stage $4$.

$\begin{array}{c|cccc}\text{Stage}&1&2&3&4\\\hline\text{Matchsticks}&\square&\square&\square&\square\end{array}$
workedExamples.solution_text:
Each new square adds $4$ matchsticks. Multiply the number of squares by $4$.

$\begin{aligned}1\times4&=4\\2\times4&=8\\3\times4&=12\\4\times4&=16\end{aligned}$

Record each count beneath its stage number.

$\begin{array}{c|cccc}\text{Stage}&1&2&3&4\\\hline\text{Matchsticks}&4&8&12&16\end{array}$

workedExamples.question_text:
A growing pattern has one group of $8$ tiles for each stage number. Its table shows $16$ tiles at stage $2$.

Complete the entries for stages $4$ and $7$.

$\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Stage}&2&4&7\\\hline\text{Tiles}&16&\square&\square\end{array}$
workedExamples.solution_text:
Stage $4$ has $4$ groups of $8$ tiles. Stage $7$ has $7$ groups.

$\begin{aligned}4\times8&=32\\7\times8&=56\end{aligned}$

$\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Stage}&2&4&7\\\hline\text{Tiles}&16&32&56\end{array}$

The stage numbers skip ahead, so each column must use its own number of groups.

foundation.question_text:
A pattern has $1$, $2$, then $3$ separate triangles.
Each triangle has $3$ counters.
Complete the table for stages $1$ to $3$.

At each stage, a pattern has that many rows of $4$ beads.
Record the bead counts for stages $1$, $2$, $3$ and $4$.

A tile pattern shows $5$ tiles in each group, starts with one group at stage $1$ and adds one new group at every stage.
Fill the counts for stages $1$ to $3$.

Each stage has its stage number of separate hexagons, with $6$ marked corners on each.
Build a table for stages $1$ to $4$.

A pattern uses $7$ dots in each column, starts with one column at stage $1$ and adds one column per stage.
What row of dot counts belongs under stages $1$, $2$ and $3$?

A design has $8$ small squares in each strip and one strip for each stage.
Record the totals through stage $4$.

development.question_text:
A pattern has $9$ pegs in each ring and one ring per stage.
Complete $\begin{array}{c|cccc}\text{Stage}&2&3&4&5\\\hline\text{Pegs}&18&\square&36&\square\end{array}$.

Each panel contains $12$ tiles.
Make a table of the number of tiles in $1$, $3$, $5$ and $7$ panels.

A dot design has as many spokes as its stage number, with $11$ dots per spoke.
Complete the table for stages $2$, $4$ and $6$.

A pattern uses $14$ counters per frame and has as many frames as its stage number.
Complete the table at stages $3$, $6$ and $9$.

A mosaic has $15$ tiles in each repeated block and as many blocks as its stage number.
Complete the table for stages $2$, $4$ and $6$.

Each shape in a pattern has $13$ marked points, and the pattern has as many separate shapes as its stage number.
Extend the table from stage $4$ to stages $5$ and $6$: $\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Stage}&4&5&6\\\hline\text{Points}&52&\square&\square\end{array}$.

mastery.question_text:
A stage-$n$ display consists of $n$ separate stars, each with $16$ lights.
Build a table for stages $2$, $5$, $8$ and $10$.

A pattern has as many groups as its stage number, with $18$ counters per group.
Complete the table for stages $1$, $2$, $3$ and $4$.

A bead pattern has as many sections as its stage number, with $24$ beads per section.
Complete the table for stages $3$ and $7$.
